tagline: A small, quiet island in Trat with white sand and clear water — flat enough to cycle, with snorkeling on nearby islands and a low-carbon way of life
introHtml:
Koh Mak is a small island in Trat province, sitting between Koh Chang and Koh Kood. It's peaceful and fairly flat, so you can easily get around by bicycle or motorbike, and it's known for its low-carbon, eco-conscious approach to tourism. People come to Koh Mak to slow down and relax — there's no busy nightlife here.

The main beaches are Ao Kao on the south side, with shallow clear water, white sand, and lovely sunsets, and Ao Suan Yai on the north side, which is longer and quieter. Another highlight is taking a boat out to snorkel at nearby Koh Kham and the clear waters of Koh Rang. If you like simple island life — cycling past coconut and rubber plantations and falling asleep to the sound of the waves — Koh Mak is a great fit. Honesty: Koh Mak is a long trip to reach, and many places close during the May–October monsoon. Things cost more on the island than on the mainland, and shops and services are limited, so bring your essentials and cash.
bestTime: November–April, when the sea is clear and calm — best for swimming, snorkeling, and cycling, and the island is fully open. May–October is monsoon season with rough seas, when many guesthouses and boats close.

highlights.name: Ao Kao Beach
highlights.blurb: The main beach on the south side of Koh Mak, with white sand and shallow clear water good for swimming. There are resorts and beachfront spots, and beautiful sunsets with Koh Kood in the distance.

highlights.name: Ao Suan Yai Beach
highlights.blurb: A long beach on the north side that's quieter and more private, with white sand and clear water. It has resorts and a pier, ideal if you want a calm, relaxing stay.

highlights.name: Cycling around the island
highlights.blurb: Koh Mak is flat, so it's easy to cycle or ride a motorbike past coconut groves, rubber plantations, and the various beaches. It's one of the island's real charms.

highlights.name: Snorkeling at Koh Kham
highlights.blurb: A small island near Koh Mak with clear water and coral right off the beach. You can take a boat over to snorkel and swim in a single day — a popular spot on the water.

highlights.name: Low-carbon tourism
highlights.blurb: Koh Mak champions eco-conscious travel that cuts down on waste and energy use. Visitors are asked to carry their trash back out and not disturb the natural surroundings.

highlights.name: Quiet island atmosphere
highlights.blurb: With no busy nightlife, Koh Mak suits anyone who wants to relax slowly — falling asleep to the waves, reading a book, and cycling around at an easy pace.

foodScene.name: Fresh seafood
foodScene.note: Koh Mak has seafood spots along the beaches and at resorts, serving shrimp, shellfish, crab, and fish cooked fresh at reasonable prices. Eat by the sea and catch the breeze.

foodScene.name: Beachfront spots and small bars
foodScene.note: Ao Kao has beachside spots and bars where you can sit, eat, and have a drink while watching the sunset. The vibe is quiet and easygoing — no rowdy parties.

foodScene.name: Small cafes
foodScene.note: The island has small cafes serving fresh coffee and desserts scattered along the beaches — a good place to stop and rest while cycling around.

foodScene.name: Local and made-to-order food
foodScene.note: The village has made-to-order and local eateries at local prices — a cheaper option than the resort restaurants, with bold flavors and good value.

attractions.name: Ao Kao Beach
attractions.blurb: The main beach on the south side, with white sand and shallow clear water good for swimming. There are resorts and beachfront spots, with lovely sunsets and views of Koh Kood.

attractions.name: Ao Suan Yai Beach
attractions.blurb: A long, quiet, private beach on the north side, with white sand and clear water. It has resorts and a pier — ideal for a calm, relaxing stay.

attractions.name: Koh Kham
attractions.blurb: A small island near Koh Mak with clear water and coral off the beach. Take a boat over to snorkel and swim in a single day — a popular spot on the water.

attractions.name: Cycling around the island
attractions.blurb: The island is flat, so it's easy to cycle past coconut groves, rubber plantations, and the various beaches. It's the standout activity on Koh Mak.

attractions.name: Ao Nid village and pier
attractions.blurb: The Ao Nid pier area and village, with restaurants, bike rentals, and the simple island way of life — the main spot for catching boats on and off the island.

attractions.name: Viewpoints and sunsets
attractions.blurb: Ao Kao and the seaside spots around the island are great corners for watching the sunset and photographing the calm, pretty sea.

attractions.name: Snorkeling the nearby islands
attractions.blurb: Take a boat out to snorkel at Koh Kham and Koh Rang, where the water is clear and there's coral — a popular sea trip from Koh Mak on calm-water days.
